title: "Tie-back: (In)dependence and Information"

## Removal Is Measurement, Run Backward

Chapter 1 asked *how much* two variables move together.  This chapter asked how
to *cancel* that movement.  They are the same object seen from two sides:

| | [Measure](../dependence/index.qmd) (Ch. 1) | Remove (Ch. 4) |
|---|---|---|
| Question | how dependent are $X$ and $Y$? | make $\hat y$ independent of $S$ |
| Tool | a dependence measure $\operatorname{Dep}$ | the *same* measure, as a penalty |
| Output | a number | a model on the trade-off frontier |

Every rung of the removal ladder is a measurement rung used as a loss:

```
loss = fit(y_hat, y) + mu * Dep(y_hat, S)
                            └────────────┘
                     a Chapter-1 measure, differentiated
```

## The Two Roads, Once More

The dependence chapter's fork — *do you need the distribution?* — reappears,
now about *removing* rather than measuring:

```
Do you need the density to remove the dependence?
│
├── NO  →  kernel removal:  Dep = CKA / HSIC(y_hat, S)
│          no density, differentiable, bounded — the workhorse
│
└── YES →  information removal:  Dep = MI / total correlation
           needs a learned density → Gaussianization / flows
```

The kernel road is the practical default; the information road reconnects
fairness to [Gaussianization](../gaussianization/index.qmd) — but it must be
**conditional** (Gaussianize $\hat y$ given $S$) to yield a fair model, as the
[Gaussianize-first lab](labs/lab-tool2.5-gaussianize-first.qmd) shows; marginal
or joint Gaussianization alone is not enough.

::: {#cell-fig-shape-removed .cell execution_count=2}
``` {.python .cell-code}
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(8, 3.6))
rungs = ["drop\nfeature", "linear\n(cka_linear)", "CKA\n(cka_rbf)",
         "adversarial"]
removes_line = [0, 1, 1, 1]
removes_curve = [0, 0, 1, 1]
xpos = np.arange(len(rungs))
ax.bar(xpos - 0.18, removes_line, width=0.36, color=COOL, label="removes the line")
ax.bar(xpos + 0.18, removes_curve, width=0.36, color=CRASH,
       label="removes the curve")
ax.set_xticks(xpos); ax.set_xticklabels(rungs, fontsize=10)
ax.set_yticks([0, 1]); ax.set_yticklabels(["no", "yes"])
ax.set_title("Pick the cheapest Dep that sees what you fear", fontsize=12)
ax.legend(fontsize=9, frameon=False, loc="center right")
despine(ax)
fig.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```

## The Through-Line
The **transform** that threads the measurement ladder threads this one too: a
hand-picked map (ranks, kernels) on the no-density road, a learned invertible map
(Gaussianization) on the density road.  Measuring it, removing it, and — next —
*propagating* it are one operation seen three ways.
:::

## Hand-Off

You can now force a model to be blind to a chosen variable — fairness and
factor-neutrality, one operation.  The companion move is to stop *removing*
dependence and start **propagating** it: carrying uncertainty and risk through a
model, where the same Gaussianization machine runs *backward* to generate
scenarios.  See [Uncertainty](../uncertainty/index.qmd).

The hands-on [labs](labs/index.qmd) put all of this on real data: a credit model
neutralized against `sex`, and a strategy neutralized against the market.
